newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Bund volatility heads up amid put buying.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Bund volatility heads up amid put buying.

text.p: Implied volatility of Bund options traded on LIFFE drifted higher on Monday as investors sought protection against reversals of the recent rally, traders said.
"It's not up on heavy buying," said a trader at a Swiss bank in London. "But volatility is looking relatively cheap and people are looking to buy protection."
Volatility of November serial options on the December futures contract rose to 4.65-4.71 percent, after closing around 4.43 percent on Friday.
December volatility was up slightly at 4.85 percent, compared with a previous close of 4.65.
December Bund futures were off 0.27 at 99.43 by 1215 GMT, after setting a new contract high of 99.76 on Friday.
A broker at a British brokerage said volume was subdued after Friday's excitement, with put trading the predominant activity throughout the series.
Traders said the 98.50 strike puts were active, with more than 1,200 contracts traded at that strike in November, and more than 900 in December.
"It's mostly been plain vanilla put buying," said the trader at the Swiss bank. "There have been some put spreads, but not really many complicated trades."
The broker said call options were not attracting much attention, after they had dominated activity last week ahead of the key U.S. non-farm payrolls data on Friday.
The report showed a fall of 40,000 jobs in September, compared with expectations of a rise of 166,000, and led to a global debt rally.
On Friday, traders said more than 10,000 November calls were traded at the 99.50 strike. They said the trades were done mostly by one U.S. house and one large British brokerage.
